propositions: A DC transport built on pycontribs/jira must be confined to an opt-in [jira-datacenter] extra, imported lazily inside functions that need it, so rebar's import-free contract is preserved and missing-extra raises a clear install-naming error.

The DC transport's every method returns raw payload shapes (dicts) that rebar's existing mappers already consume, unwrapping the pycontribs object model at the boundary so downstream code never sees jira.Issue instances.

TLS verification is never disabled; the transport rejects non-https base_url with ConfigError unless allow_insecure=true is set, and a verification failure names the ca_bundle setting rather than silently proceeding.
The DC transport must self-register into the _backend_registry by importing it in adapters/__init__.py, so select_backend('jira-datacenter') resolves at runtime without BackendRegistryError.

An HTTP error is attempted exactly once (not retried) while connection timeouts are retried with documented 2s/5s backoff, mirroring acli_rest behavior including builtin TimeoutError for ssl/socket read-timeout.

NameIdentity user-search lookup is wired to a live search_users call against the DC instance, returning authoritative identity for existing users and raising BackendAssigneeNotFoundError for unknown ones, closing a wire J4 deliberately left dangling.
